How it started

KabirBrewCafe didn’t start with a business plan. It started with an oven — a wood-fired oven that a friend brought back from a trip to Naples, and a question: why isn’t there a place in Netrang that does pizza the way it’s supposed to taste?

The answer was: there wasn’t. So we built one. A small space in Jin Bazar, a second-hand espresso machine, and a menu small enough to fit on one page. The first year was all word of mouth. The second year, word had spread.

Good ingredients,
no shortcuts

The dough is made fresh every morning — flour, water, salt, yeast, and time. The sauce is just San Marzano tomatoes, crushed by hand. The mozzarella is shredded daily. Nothing comes out of a bag.

Same goes for the coffee. Single-origin beans, ground to order, pulled shot by shot. And the margaritas? Fresh lime, good tequila, no syrups. It’s not complicated. It’s just doing simple things properly.

“Simple things, done properly, every day.”

That’s the whole philosophy. No secret recipes, no gimmicks. Just a wood-fired oven, good coffee beans, and people who care.

A place you want
to stay at

The front room is warm and compact — a few tables, the open kitchen, the oven glowing in the corner. Out back, there’s a small courtyard with string lights and enough room for groups.

It’s the kind of space where conversations linger. Where the background noise is clinking glasses and the low hum of the espresso machine. Where “one coffee” turns into “okay, maybe a margarita too.”
